_: Shared access-code SHAPE vectors. The portal (IapRepository::normalizeAccessCode) and the apps
(VpnHood.Core.Toolkit AccessCodeUtils.Validate) must agree exactly: a code one accepts and the
other refuses is a person who cannot use a code they legitimately hold. They drifted once —
the portal required all-digits while the apps allow letters after the checksum.
A TWIN OF THIS FILE lives at VpnHood/tests/VpnHood.Test/Fixtures/access-code-vectors.json and
must stay identical. The repos ship separately, so it is copied rather than referenced; both
suites read their copy, so a change on one side fails the other's tests.

valid.why: all digits, as the access manager issues them
separators are decoration and are stripped
letters are legal after the checksum — it sums character codes
lowercase too, and case is never folded
a repeated letter still has to check out

invalid.why: the checksum position must be a digit
checksum does not match the rest
one character changed, so the checksum no longer matches
a separator is stripped, leaving 19 characters
